mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or equivalent competent corporate registry in the jurisdiction of the ultimate parent shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication: (A) Hague Apostille route: notarization by a public notary in the country of issuance, followed by application for an Apostille certificate from the designated competent authority (usually the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or equivalent) in that country; no consular legalization is required when the destination state is an Apostille Convention member. (B) Consular Legalization route (only when the destination state is not an Apostille Convention member): notarization, then authentication by the competent foreign affairs authority in the country of issuance, and final legalization by the Embassy or Consulate of the destination state in the country of issuance. Routes (A) and (B) are parallel and mutually exclusive; neither route uses the other's steps in sequence.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every ultimate beneficial owner, director, senior manager, and authorized signatory must be screened against the People's Bank of China (PBOC) sanctions and money-laundering risk lists, the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) list and Sectoral Sanctions Identifications (SSI) list, and the applicable domestic sanctions list maintained by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China. Enhanced due diligence shall also include politically exposed person (PEP) identification using governmental positions databases, adverse media and integrity searches, criminal record verification, and corroboration of the source of funds and wealth. The screening is executed at on-boarding, upon any material change in control or governance, and via continuous automated alerts at least every 24 hours. Any hit or unresolved alert requires escalation to senior compliance management and, where required, filing of a suspicious transaction report with the PBOC's China Anti-Money Laundering Monitoring and Analysis Center.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Name Registration System of the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Chinese company names must follow a four-tier structure: administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or business feature, and legal form. The registered name must be in simplified Chinese characters; pinyin romanization is not accepted as the legal registered name. A corresponding English name may be used for banking, tax, and foreign trade filings but must be a faithful phonetic transliteration of the Chinese trade name and must remain consistent across all corporate documents and government registrations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within fifteen calendar days after the SAMR notifies a rejection of the proposed company name, the applicant may file a written administrative reconsideration request with the superior market regulatory authority, attaching the rejection notice, a statutory brief explaining why the name does not violate prohibited-token rules, and an alternative compliant name. The authority must decide within thirty calendar days. If the reconsideration upholds the original refusal, the applicant may commence an administrative lawsuit before the competent People's Court within six months. A new online name reservation can be made immediately to protect a revised name, and expedited communication with local registration staff is recommended to align with the SAMR's internal guidelines.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible for a China WFOE operating as a special purpose acquisition and holding vehicle. The State Administration for Market Regulation and local tax authorities require the registered address to be an actual physical site within the registered jurisdiction, with a lease or ownership certificate, a visible plaque, and the capacity to receive official legal and tax correspondence. Corporate banks additionally reject virtual offices during account opening because they fail the know-your-customer visit and physical presence requirements. A shell or blank-check entity without a real office faces a high probability of having its registration challenged by the SAMR and the tax bureau as a fictitious address, which may lead to freezing of tax status and inability to open bank accounts.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical inspection risk for this SPAC blank-check entity is quantified at approximately 40% in the first eighteen months and drops to 10-15% if a substantive local office is maintained. Checklist used by SAMR and municipal tax authorities includes: (1) a matching company signboard and premises at the registered address; (2) availability of a legal representative or personnel able to receive official notices; (3) presence of the company seal and security custody; (4) availability of accounting books, invoices, and incorporation filings; and (5) proper maintenance of the bank statement or capital verification records. Any failed inspection or vacant-address finding triggers an administrative inquiry, fines, and potential removal from the registry.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision), as amended, particularly Articles 23, 24-27, 29-32, 46, 49-50, 57-58, 66-68, 72, 89, 92 and 108-111; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 2, 4, 6, 13, 14, 19, 22 and 31; Regulations on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (State Council Order No. 746, 2021), Articles 2, 8, 9, 15, 16, 17 and 20; Provisions on the Administration of Foreign-Invested Companies; and the Administrative Measures for Overseas Securities Offering and Listing Filing by Domestic Enterprises, if and when public-market SPAC activity is commenced.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Market Entity Registration Administration of the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), acting through the local Municipal or Provincial Administration for Market Regulation at the registered place of the WFOE, via the National Integrated Enterprise Registration Portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign-Invested Company Establishment Registration Application Form (Unified Social Credit Code Registration) submitted through the SAMR enterprise registration online platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None for an ordinary WFOE limited liability company; the PRC Company Law (2023 Revision) has abolished the statutory minimum paid-up capital threshold for non-licensed industries. The articles of association must state the subscribed registered capital and the contribution schedule, and the sole shareholder must complete the paid-in contribution within the statutory five-year period from establishment unless a shorter schedule is agreed in the SPAC sponsor agreement. There is no mandatory blocked escrow account as a Companies Act incorporation condition; however, for SPAC operations, a segregated trust or escrow account must be established with a licensed PRC commercial bank or qualified custodian in accordance with the escrow agreement and the relevant securities listing or public-market financing requirements before any public-market funds are deposited.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [CN_WFOE_LTD]

WHEREAS, the Company is a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company incorporated under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China; and

WHEREAS, the Company has been formed to function as a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC), blank-check vehicle and investment holding entity for public market merger and acquisition transactions; and

WHEREAS, the Board of Directors has been lawfully appointed by the sole shareholder and has resolved to approve all arrangements necessary for the exercise of corporate powers and the opening of business.

NOW, THEREFORE, the Board of Directors adopts the following resolutions:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND VERIFICATION. RESOLVED, that the sole shareholder's subscription of the entire registered capital of the Company be and hereby is approved, accepted and confirmed. The registered capital of the Company is [INSERT AMOUNT] RMB, divided into [INSERT NUMBER] ordinary shares of a single class, having a par value of [INSERT PAR VALUE] RMB per share. The Board directs the Chief Financial Officer to verify all bank receipts for the paid-in portion, to record the contribution in the shareholders' register, and to ensure that actual contributions are completed no later than five years from the date of establishment as required by the Company Law. The Board also directs that the capital contribution report be filed with the competent market regulation authority and through the foreign investment information reporting platform.

2. BANKING AND ESCROW AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the Company shall maintain a basic operating account, a capital verification account, and, for SPAC purposes, a segregated trust and escrow account with a licensed commercial bank in the People's Republic of China. The Board hereby authorizes the General Manager and the Chief Financial Officer, jointly or as otherwise required by the executed bank mandate, to open, operate, pledge and close all bank accounts, to execute SWIFT wire transfer instructions, and to sign all escrow disbursement instructions; provided, however, that any release of escrow funds shall require a separate board resolution and compliance with the applicable SPAC trust agreement.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. RESOLVED, that the registered office located at [INSERT FULL ADDRESS], People's Republic of China, is adopted as the statutory domicile and principal office of the Company. The Board directs that the lease contract, ownership certificate or occupancy certificate, and landlord consent letter be maintained at the registered office and that legal process and regulatory notices be received at that address.

4. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. RESOLVED, that [INSERT NAME] is appointed as Director and General Manager, [INSERT NAME] is appointed as Chief Financial Officer, and [INSERT NAME] is appointed as Corporate Secretary, each to serve until removal or replacement by the Board or the sole shareholder. Each officer is authorized, within the limits of the articles of association, to execute contracts, bank forms, filings and any other instruments needed to comply with these resolutions.

5. DELEGATION AND GOVERNANCE. RESOLVED, that the Board delegates day-to-day operations to the appointed officers, adopts the corporate seal policy, and authorizes the use of the company seal in accordance with the articles. All litigation, arbitration, tax, regulatory and material contractual documents shall bear the company seal and signatures as prescribed by the seal policy. This resolution is effective immediately and shall remain in full force until amended or revoked by a subsequent board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Negative List Compliance Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR Online Name Reservation Module and local Municipal Administration for Market Regulation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online application through the SAMR name reservation module for the proposed Chinese-language and English-language names of the WFOE and the SPAC vehicle. The application must demonstrate that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing enterprise name and contains no prohibited terms. Prior to formal submission, screen the proposed business scope against the Foreign Investment Access Negative List issued by the National Development and Reform Commission and the Ministry of Commerce to confirm that special purpose acquisition activities are neither prohibited nor restricted. The name reservation notice is valid for six months. The applicant should also verify that the proposed SPAC scope does not trigger pre-approval under the Measures for the Administration of Overseas Securities Offering and Listing of Domestic Enterprises; if it does, a pre-filing clearance comment should be sought before incorporation to avoid post-registration restructuring.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation application
Foreign investor legal existence certificate or passport copy
Proposed articles of association and business scope summary
Negative-list compliance self-assessment memorandum
Power of attorney appointing the local registration agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried, the applicant should file an amended application with up to three distinct alternative names, or narrow the business scope and resubmit the negative-list compliance memorandum. Name objections from third parties must be answered within the local public objection period; a written response with prior-use evidence and goodwill statement is recommended.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Notarization and Authentication of Formation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary office in the investor's home jurisdiction; Chinese consular authority or Apostille competent authority; SAMR local administration for pre-review
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the articles of association, the written shareholder decision, the board composition statement and the appointment certificate for the legal representative. Foreign investor documents, including certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing and passport of the ultimate shareholder, must be notarized and authenticated either by apostille under the Hague Apostille Convention or by Chinese consular legalization where the investor jurisdiction is not yet party to the convention, and all foreign language documents must be accompanied by an official Chinese translation prepared by a licensed translation company. The articles must state the company name, registered address, registered capital, contribution method and deadline, governance structure, legal representative name, board composition and the permitted financial SPAC purpose. The electronic dossier is pre-reviewed on the SAMR online platform, and scanned originals may be accepted unless an on-site interview or paper countersignature is ordered by the local authority.
required_dossiers: Notarized and authenticated foreign investor certificate and passport
Official Chinese translation of foreign investor documents
Signed articles of association
Board resolution regarding company formation
Appointment documents for legal representative, directors, supervisors and manager
Lease contract, real estate certificate or landlord consent for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or authentication officer requires additional evidence, obtain the missing corporate incumbency certificate or updated apostille from the home-country registry within 15 days. If the articles of association are returned for correction, adopt amending articles and submit the corrected version within the statutory 30-day window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment Registration Submission and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Market Entity Registration Bureau under SAMR, via the National Enterprise Registration Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the SAMR National Enterprise Registration Portal and submit the signed registration application, articles of association, name reservation notice, lease certificate, landlord consent, and identification documents of the legal representative, directors, supervisors and manager. The system will verify the unified social credit code and issue an electronic business license after approval. On approval, the applicant must arrange the engraving of the company seal, legal representative seal, financial seal and invoice seal at a Public Security Bureau licensed seal engraver, and file the seals with the local public security organ. The company must then complete tax registration, social insurance registration and statistical registration through the integrated post-registration portal before carrying out any revenue-generating operation. The physical business license must be displayed at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Approved name reservation notice
Completed establishment registration application form
Signed articles of association
Apostilled or legalized foreign investor documents
Lease contract and landlord consent letter
Identity documents of legal representative, directors, supervisors and manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration application is suspended, an online rectification notice will specify the missing documents; the applicant should cure and resubmit within 30 days. If the business license has already been issued but contains a typographical error, file a name-correction registration and follow the quick-change procedure at the same SAMR window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening, SAFE Foreign Exchange Filing and Capital Injection
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in China; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through the bank's cross-border capital information system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the business license, the legal representative or authorized agent shall physically attend the licensed commercial bank to open the RMB basic deposit account and the foreign currency capital account. The bank must complete the People's Bank of China account record-filing and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) foreign direct investment (FDI) registration through the bank's cross-border capital information system before the foreign shareholder wires the registered capital. The Board shall deliver the board resolution authorizing the banking relationship, the sealed articles, the business license and the directors' identification. The bank will verify the remittance details and issue the foreign currency registration notice. Paid-up capital must be deposited to the capital account and, once received, the company must file the paid-in capital record with SAMR. For SPAC operations, the company must simultaneously establish a segregated escrow or trust account under a board-approved escrow agreement with the same bank or a qualifying custodian; no public-market funds may be accepted until the escrow is effective.
required_dossiers: Business license (original)
Company seal, legal representative seal and financial seal
Articles of association and board resolution authorizing bank accounts
Legal representative passport or identity document and eligibility certificate
SAFE Foreign Direct Investment registration questionnaire
SPAC escrow or trust agreement (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or SAFE rejects the FDI registration, the company should provide additional evidence of beneficial ownership, a cleared source-of-funds statement, and a revised board resolution; the application can be resubmitted through the bank within 20 business days. If the capital contribution deadline cannot be met, the articles should be amended to extend the contribution period before the five-year deadline expires.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Governance, Regulatory Notifications and Occupancy Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR local administration; Ministry of Commerce via integrated foreign investment information reporting; China Securities Regulatory Commission if listing filing is triggered; local fire rescue brigade for office occupancy
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within thirty days after business license issuance, file the Foreign Investment Information Report through the integrated marketplace authority platform, and, if applicable, make the initial securities listing filing or negative-list exposure declaration with the China Securities Regulatory Commission under the Domestic Enterprise Overseas Offering and Listing Filing Administrative Measures. Convene the first board meeting to approve the pro-forma resolutions, adopt the seal policy, approve the banking mandate, ratify the registered office and confirm the officers' powers. The SPAC vehicle must also complete an office fire safety inspection sign-off from the local fire rescue brigade for the registered office and obtain a building occupancy compliance certificate from the property owner. If the SPAC will engage in trust or escrow management, the custodian bank shall provide the final escrow operational compliance letter and include it in the corporate records. All completed filings shall be consolidated in the statutory corporate book.
required_dossiers: First board meeting minutes
Foreign investment information report confirmation
Business license and sealed corporate matrix
CSRC filing confirmation or legal opinion (if public listing is imminent)
Office lease and fire safety inspection certificate
Final escrow operational compliance letter (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the foreign investment information report or CSRC filing is queried, the company should respond with the corrected shareholding structure, business scope description and capital contribution evidence within 15 days. If the fire safety inspection fails, undertake the fire rectification work ordered by the brigade and request re-inspection before moving into the premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no industrial licensing authority applies to ISIC 6499 (Special Purpose Acquisition Company). This entity has no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing operations. Any financial regulatory coordination is handled separately by SAMR, SAFE and, once public-market activity begins, the China Securities Regulatory Commission.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable to industrial operations. No dedicated industrial operating permit is triggered by this blank-check SPAC WFOE. Statutory financial and commercial compliance for the entity is limited to foreign investment reporting, SAFE FDI registration, CSRC overseas listing filing if applicable, and the trust or escrow arrangement; these are not industrial operating licenses.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) local bureau is not triggered for an administrative office-based SPAC with no construction or polluting processes.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater discharge, volatile organic compound emissions, hazardous waste generation, or other quantitative pollutant thresholds are triggered by ISIC 6499 administrative financial activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable as an industrial civil defense permit. For office occupancy, the WFOE must obtain the landlord's fire safety inspection certificate issued by the local fire rescue brigade and the building occupancy certificate from the property owner; these are tenancy and occupational safety compliance documents, not industrial civil defense or structural load approvals.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA) with local State Tax Service bureaus; online filing via the China Electronic Tax Administration portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. The WFOE obtains a Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) from the State Administration for Market Regulation at incorporation; under the multi-license integration system this USCC is automatically the national tax identification number (TIN/VAT ID). 2. Within 30 calendar days of business license issuance, the WFOE must complete supplementary tax registration information (legal representative, accounting system, bank account, VAT taxpayer status election) through the China Electronic Tax Administration portal; no separate tax registration certificate is issued. 3. A foreign non-resident parent/shareholder is not required to obtain a Chinese TIN solely for equity ownership in the WFOE. 4. If the non-resident entity derives China-source income without a permanent establishment, the local payer or withholding agent must complete simplified non-resident tax withholding registration with the STA and obtain a non-resident taxpayer identification code before remittance. 5. If the non-resident entity maintains a permanent establishment in China outside the WFOE, it must separately register as a non-resident enterprise under the STA jurisdiction where the PE is located.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. China does not operate a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election system for a WFOE; the entity is always taxed at entity level under the Enterprise Income Tax Law. The only elective feature relevant for indirect tax is the choice between small-scale VAT taxpayer treatment and general VAT taxpayer treatment, which is available only where turnover remains below the RMB 5,000,000 general taxpayer threshold.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no turnover threshold for the WFOE to become VAT-registered: incorporation automatically creates tax registration obligations. Mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration applies once annual taxable turnover exceeds RMB 5,000,000; below that amount small-scale VAT taxpayer treatment may apply. Financial services supplied by the SPAC vehicle are generally taxable at 6% under the services rate while the general headline VAT rate for goods is 13%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Golden Tax Phase IV requires all VAT invoices to be issued through the STA national electronic invoice service platform with real-time fiscal clearance. Each invoice must carry a unique digital invoice code and an anti-fraud cryptographic digital stamp generated by the platform. WFOEs must integrate their billing/ERP systems with the STA e-invoice API for immediate transmission of invoice issuance, cancellation, red-flag reversal and exception reporting; fully-digitised electronic invoices are the national standard and legacy offline tax-control invoices are being phased out.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods zero-rating applies when tangible goods are physically exported from China under a customs export declaration, the sale is made to a non-resident buyer, and export foreign exchange proceeds are repatriated to China within the statutory collection period. Cross-border services, including offshore digital services, qualify for 0% VAT where the service recipient is outside China, the service is wholly consumed outside China, and contemporaneous contracts, performance evidence and foreign currency settlement records are retained. A SPAC-related financial service is zero-rated only where the entire transaction counterparty, underlying economic activity and consumption occur outside China and the STA recognises the offshore supply under cross-border service tax rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: China Customs Export Declaration (Customs Bill of Export) lodged through the China International Trade Single Window
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from China and arrival in the overseas destination
Commercial invoice, packing list and export sales contract signed by the WFOE
Bank-issued foreign exchange receipt voucher and SAFE trade-in-foreign-exchange declaration record evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA Golden Tax IV system reconciles customs export declarations, VAT invoice data, transport documents, bank receipts and SAFE foreign exchange records. If zero-rating is unsubstantiated, STA retroactively reverses the 0% VAT rate, assesses output VAT at the domestic rate, claws back any VAT refund already paid, imposes daily late-payment surcharge and administrative fines for tax maladministration under the Law on Administration of Tax Collection, and refers deliberate cases for criminal prosecution under the Criminal Law provisions on fraudulent export tax rebates. Liability may extend to the WFOE's legal representative, finance officer and beneficial shareholders where fraud or false documentation is proven.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese Mainland maintains a split current and capital account FX regime. Current account receipts and payments, including trade-related settlements and service fees, are fully convertible and may be effected through designated domestic banks without SAFE pre-approval, provided the transaction is genuine and supported by customary underlying documentation. Capital account items, however, remain heavily controlled; all inbound equity investment into a WFOE, outbound acquisition disbursements, and external borrowing must be registered with SAFE under the FDI protocol and, where relevant, under PBOC foreign debt rules. Registered capital of a SPAC-oriented WFOE may be denominated in RMB or foreign currency; once foreign currency capital is received, it must be settled into RMB through the designated bank's capital account system and monitored for compliance with the negative list governing settlement use. Profit remittance to offshore investors is permitted after annual statutory audit, tax clearance, and confirmation of registered capital paid-in; remittance is processed through current account channels but banks require audit reports, tax certificates, board resolutions, and foreign exchange registration certificates. Access to onshore FX markets for hedging is limited to real exposures evidenced by contracts or a valid underlying investment file, and speculative derivatives are prohibited. The overall regime is therefore workable for a genuine SPAC vehicle but demands documentary discipline, pre-registration with SAFE, and strict sponsorship of every capital step.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Goods-trade export proceeds must be repatriated into China within 180 days from the date of customs declaration. No fixed statutory percentage of export proceeds is required to be mandatorily converted into RMB; the surrender ratio is effectively zero after recent liberalisation, but any export receipts retained in foreign currency must be held in an approved current-account FX account at a designated domestic bank and must be supported by trade-invoice and shipping documentation. The enterprise is also required to perform foreign exchange receipt and payment declaration through the bank's reporting system before settlement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability rating: Low; effectively prohibited. Offshore fintech EMIs and digital challenger banks are not viable as primary banking rails for a Mainland WFOE. They are legally barred from holding a PBOC banking licence or CNAPS settlement membership, do not have access to SAFE foreign exchange registration, and cannot provide a lawful RMB clearing path for registered capital or trade disbursements. Such EMIs can only act as auxiliary tooling for offshore parent-company balances in permitted jurisdictions; the SPAC vehicle's onshore operating, capital, and escrow accounts must remain at a licensed Chinese commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: PBOC counter-opening rules require the statutory legal representative to complete at least one face-to-face identity confirmation at the bank or through SAFE/PBOC accredited remote video confirmation before a WFOE basic deposit account becomes active. A remote consular proxy opening is possible in narrow circumstances: a foreign director may execute and notarise a board resolution abroad, have it legalised by the PRC embassy/consulate or apostilled where China recognises the Hague Apostille Convention, and authorise a locally appointed finance officer to appear physically in-branch with the corporate chop; however, Tier-1 banks still dispatch a relationship manager to the registered office for an on-site visit and may require an in-person interview with the controlling director or UBO before activating online banking.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layered SPAC promoter structure with multiple offshore holding vehicles obscuring the natural-person ultimate beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate ownership diagram from the SPAC promoter to each natural person, certified copies of shareholders registers and trust deeds, passport copies, source-of-wealth statements, fund proof for all equity contributions, and independent counsel opinion confirming the UBO chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-operating shell entity with no local employees, no business address, and no economic activity other than holding IPO or escrow cash
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: WFOE lease agreement, payroll and employer social-security filings, board-approved business plan and acquisition mandate, SPAC trust agreement showing escrow custody, detailed cash-flow forecast, and a signed statutory declaration on the intended use of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from offshore banks where the sponsor and investor identities do not match the SAFE FDI registration and the remitting party is not the registered shareholder
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE foreign investment registration certificate, bank-to-bank MT103 trail to the registered FDI shareholder, notarised board approval of the capital call, investor AML/KYC files, fund-source evidence such as audited financial statements or brokerage statements, and an undertaking that all remitters are the registered contributors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk outbound disbursements to acquisition targets and unknown beneficiaries through the SPAC liquidation or trust mechanism
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed SPAC trust agreement, integrity due diligence on the acquisition target's shareholders and directors, sanctioned-entity screening results, transaction rationale memo, merger control clearance where applicable, and an escrow payout instruction countersigned by the independent trustee.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital must arrive via SWIFT MT103 from the registered offshore shareholder or the SPAC trust custodian holding IPO proceeds, with the remittance field indicating the SAFE FDI registration number and the transaction purpose code for direct investment capital contribution. The receiving Tier-1 bank will validate the remittance against the capital contribution list filed under the FDI registration, perform the foreign exchange receipt declaration, and then settle into RMB through the bank's capital account supervision system; the settlement must be applied exclusively to the approved business scope and must not be used for prohibited negative-list activities such as entrusted lending, real-estate speculation, or investment into securities without an additional licence. After settlement, a Chinese registered accountant must issue a capital verification report to evidence paid-in capital and complete the market-regulator filing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational, advisory, and acquisition disbursements from the WFOE should be settled through SWIFT MT103 for direct corporate payments; commercial letters of credit via MT700 where the target transaction needs upstream documentary protection; and documentary collections for lower-risk trade-based settlements. For RMB-denominated payments within China's cross-border schemes, the bank may route through CIPS or the RMB clearing bank with an accompanying payment purpose code; all outbound transfers require a completed SAFE payment declaration, the underlying invoice or acquisition SPA copy, and where applicable the post-verification record from the bank's FX system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB/FX forward contracts linked to verified trade, capital, or foreign-currency debt obligations, executed under a SAFE-registered master agreement with a domestic Tier-1 bank.

Offshore NDFs are only permissible in the overseas parent or sponsor entity outside the WFOE, with no onshore settlement or delivery into the Mainland RMB system; the WFOE itself cannot use NDFs as a direct hedge.
Cross-currency swaps on registered external loans or SPAC-related debt instruments, limited to hedging principal and interest exposures and prohibited for speculative rebooking.
FX options used by the WFOE on a buyer-only or hedging basis when the underlying transaction has been evidenced and authorised by the bank.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Annual Report filed through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and local Market Supervision Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 in each calendar year for the immediately preceding fiscal year; newly incorporated WFOEs must file in the next full reporting window after formation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or late filing results in placement on the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Business Information; failure to remedy within three consecutive years causes transfer to the Serious Illegal and Discredited Enterprise List, triggering interdepartmental credit restrictions and potential administrative revocation of the business license, which constitutes loss of legal existence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) submitted through the integrated SAMR enterprise information publicity system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 in each calendar year for the preceding calendar year; material changes occurring after submission must be reported under the foreign-investment change-report rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit or submission of false information attracts a rectification order from SAMR or MOFCOM; refusal to rectify or material concealment may result in a fine of up to RMB 200,000, confiscation of illegal gains, referral to tax or foreign-exchange anti-avoidance authorities, and cross-departmental adverse credit consequences.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Settlement and Payment Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) through the local competent tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the end of the fiscal year, normally by May 31; if the final day falls on a statutory holiday, the deadline automatically shifts to the next working day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may incur an administrative fine of up to RMB 2,000, or RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 in serious cases, plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of overdue tax from the statutory due date; false declaration causing underpayment may trigger a penalty of 50% to 100% of the underpaid tax, while tax evasion may attract a penalty of 50% to five times the underpaid tax, asset freeze or garnishment, and ultimately administrative revocation of the business license for persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) Equity and Rights-Interests Registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through local SAFE branches or designated banks
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 in each calendar year, reporting paid-in capital, undistributed profits, accumulated earnings and ultimate beneficial ownership as of December 31 of the preceding year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Overdue or omitted registration places the WFOE on the SAFE abnormal-credit list and instructs banks to suspend routine capital-account foreign-exchange receipts and payments; repeated or serious violations may be penalized under the foreign-exchange regulations with a warning and a fine of up to RMB 300,000 and may trigger anti-money-laundering escalation, cross-border wire restrictions, and loss of foreign-exchange registration status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory independent audit by a licensed PRC CPA firm is mandatory for all WFOE limited liability companies unless the company is an exempt micro-enterprise and holds no licensed, public-interest or third-party custodial position. Audit exemption is generally available only when the enterprise satisfies all of the following simultaneously: total balance-sheet assets do not exceed RMB 10,000,000; annual operating revenue does not exceed RMB 20,000,000; and average annual headcount does not exceed 100. A SPAC blank-check vehicle maintaining trust, escrow or custodial money of third-party investors is never exempt because it holds public-interest custodial assets, carries a special-purpose acquisition license, is subject to the ISIC 6499 financial-services regulatory perimeter, and requires audited evidence for foreign-investor and foreign-exchange reporting. The audit must be performed by an accounting firm licensed by the Ministry of Finance with at least two practising CPAs registered with the Chinese Institute of Certified Public Accountants and must be completed in time to support the annual enterprise report, annual tax settlement, FDI equity registration and the foreign parent's consolidated financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS/ASBE), which are converged with IFRS. Small-scale enterprises that meet the statutory micro-enterprise tests may apply the Ministry of Finance's Small Enterprise Accounting Standards instead of full CAS; however, a SPAC WFOE with trust or escrow liabilities is expected to apply full CAS and, when consolidated by a foreign public parent, IFRS or US-GAAP-comparable reporting schedules for the parent's public filings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, the WFOE must confirm its ultimate beneficial owner and actual controller through the Enterprise Annual Report filed with SAMR, including name, nationality, identification details and shareholding percentage. Any shareholding transfer or change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be reflected in the shareholders register and approved by the shareholders or board as required by the articles of association; the company must apply to AMR for registration of the changed shareholder or registered-capital information within 30 days of the effective change, and a foreign-investment information change report must be filed with MOFCOM through SAMR within 20 working days after the transfer completion. Cross-border transfers or investments also require an updated SAFE FDI equity registration and, where applicable, escrow account documentation before any trust or acquisition funds are released.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Register of Charges/Mortgages, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - USD 2,800 per annum for registered address service, local foreign-investment secretarial agency and annual credit-report filing support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 18,000 per audit cycle for a middle-market WFOE / SPAC holding vehicle, depending on trust-escrow transaction volume, related-party disclosures, and foreign-parent IFRS or US-GAAP consolidation packages

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory incentives: (1) 15% preferential rate for qualifying High and New Technology Enterprises (HNTE); (2) 15% rate for enterprises in encouraged industries in the Western Region; (3) Small and Low-Profit Enterprise (SLPE) progressive preferential effective rates of 2.5%-5% on taxable income up to RMB 3 million for the 2023-2027 window; (4) Super deduction of research and development expenses (currently 100% of eligible R&D and 120% of deemed intangible development expenditures); (5) Particular tax holidays for new integrated circuit production projects may also be available where the SPAC invests in eligible semiconductor targets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return, Form A-type (Form A201 / 中华人民共和国企业所得税年度纳税申报表（A类）) and associated schedules (A105000 related-party transaction reporting) filed electronically via the China Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax; https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn). Quarterly provisional returns are filed on Form A200/A300 as appropriate.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual reconciliation return, supported by quarterly estimated prepayment filings (within 15 days after each quarter-end: April 15, July 15, October 15, January 15). The annual consolidated filing is due within 5 months after the tax year-end (May 31).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form A201) due by May 31 immediately following the end of the calendar fiscal year. Quarterly prepayments due by the 15th day of the fourth month following each quarter-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Operating Revenue (Row 1 of Form A-type)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate gross revenue from principal operations, including sale of goods, provision of services, trust investment and escrow interest income, sponsor management fees, listing fee income, fair value gains on IPO options/warrants, and any other business turnover, reduced by sales returns and allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All cross-border revenues from, or attributable to, affiliated non-resident enterprises must be booked at the arm's length price as verified by comparable transactions. The corresponding related-party transaction disclosure must be filed on Schedule A105000; failure to attach the schedule for intercompany service fees, debit notes, or trust management fees will trigger an automatic audit flag. Revenue from non-resident shareholders' capital contributions is not taxable, but any imputed interest on unpaid shareholder loans must be included.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales and services rendered, directly allocable depreciation, salaries of staff engaged in listing/SPAC compliance, trust custodian fees, and brokerage commissions paid to acquire or manage target businesses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Charges paid to overseas affiliates for technical, management, or advisory services must satisfy the service-TP rules (SAT Public Notice [2017] No. 6). Only actual, reasonable, and documented expenses deductible; a 20% uplift on management fees is not automatically deductible. For a SPAC WFOE, any fee paid to a non-resident sponsor or investment manager must be supported by a written contract, economic substance evidence, and withholding certificate to avoid recharacterization as constructive dividend.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxes and surcharges directly attributable to business income, including urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, property taxes on lease contracts, and stamp duty on financial instruments, excluding the CIT itself and any foreign WHT on profit repatriation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No special non-resident impact except to the extent that double tax treaty credential taxes (e.g. foreign source withholding tax on underlying interest income) are entered as taxes paid abroad and subsequently claimed on Schedule A106000 (Foreign Income Tax Credit). Ensure no double counting of the 10% WHT levied on outgoing dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial, marketing, travel, professional fees, executive compensation, board meeting costs, insurance premiums, and legal/accounting fees connected with the SPAC listing pipeline.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Service payments to directors located abroad must be treated as provision of Chinese-source services if the recipient is a tax resident of the treaty jurisdiction; withholding obligations apply at 10% (or treaty-reduced rate) on service fees. If the remuneration relates to management performed in China, it becomes Chinese-source income to the individual and requires full payroll withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Finance Costs and Fair-Value Investment Losses (Row 6-9)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest on intercompany borrowings, foreign exchange losses, impairment losses on financial assets held in trust, fair value losses on warrants or convertible debentures, and other non-operating charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to non-resident lenders is subject to the thin capitalization rule (debt-equity ratio 2:1 for all entities unless bank or financial enterprise), and WHT at 10% or treaty-reduced 7% (e.g. China-Hong Kong) on the gross interest must be withheld and declared separately. Excess interest disallowed at CIT level. Interest income earned in offshore escrow trust accounts can be taxed upon repatriation if China is the beneficial owner jurisdiction; maintain a clear breakdown in the box to avoid double taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Total Accounting Profit Before Tax (Row 13)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed as: revenue minus cost minus expenses minus losses plus non-operating income, less non-operating expenses. For a SPAC WFOE, this equals net investment income from trust securities, sponsor fees, and interest on cash deposits net of professional fees and operating overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This line is the bridge to the annual reconciliation; all previous adjustments must be reflected. Non-resident shareholders should note this is the base for determining distributable profits for dividend WHT. If the entity is treated as a 'pass-through' for treaty purposes, special anti-abuse rules (beneficial ownership) may require this to be ignored where the WFOE lacks board control over the trust assets.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit plus tax additions (e.g. non-deductible sponsor costs, excessive management fees, related-party interest exceeding thin cap) minus tax reductions (e.g. dividends from qualified resident enterprises, FTZ registered asset step-up, loss carryforwards).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Crucially, any transfer pricing adjustment under SAT Public Notice No. 42 is made here. A SPAC WFOE with zero or minimal taxable income despite large gross cash flows inside the trust will be immediately questioned. The taxpayer must file the related-party transaction transactional financial disclosures and be ready to defend with a local file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Applicable Tax Rate, Tax Payable, and Credits (Rows 17-22)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable headline rate (normally 25%; 15% if HNTE or Western Region approval) on the taxable income; subtotal income tax; less treaty/incentive reductions; less foreign tax credit; resulting actual CIT liability; less quarterly prepayments; final balance due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident investors' deemed 10% (or treaty-reduced) WHT on the post-tax earnings is not recorded on the WFOE's CIT return but on the withholding return filed in respect of outbound dividends. For a SPAC, the WFOE must ensure it obtains the TRC and beneficial ownership declaration from the non-resident shareholder before paying any distribution at a treaty-reduced WHT rate. The tax credit schedule applies to foreign income taxes paid on trust investment income earned in U.S. or Cayman escrow accounts; protect foreign tax credit evidence in the entity file.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: late surcharge of 0.05% per day on unpaid tax (Tax Collection Administration Law (TCAL) Art. 32); fixed penalty of RMB 2,000-10,000 for late filing, increasing to RMB 10,000-50,000 for serious cases (TCAL Art. 62). Underreporting or failing to pay tax via untrue invoices or related-party concealment carries 50%-5x of the tax underpaid (TCAL Art. 63); unauthorized reduction of tax base triggers 50%-5x plus inadmissibility of deductions. Criminal fraud thresholds: if underpaid tax > RMB 100,000 and exceeds 10% of the tax due, a director or legal representative will be prosecuted under Criminal Law Art. 201, punishable by up to 3 years' imprisonment (or 3-7 years in aggravated circumstances), plus fines and confiscation. The supreme tax authority will also publish serious tax defaulters and impose exit bans (blacklisting) under TCAL Art. 44.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding tax on dividends paid by a PRC-resident WFOE to a non-resident shareholder under Article 37 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law (EIT Law) and Caishui [2008] No. 1. Treaty relief: for an investor resident in a treaty jurisdiction, and holding at least 25% of the WFOE's shares for at least 12 months, the withholding rate is typically reduced to 5% (e.g., under the China-Hong Kong DTA, China-UK DTA, China-Singapore DTA). Some treaties provide 10% for portfolio investors; certain DTA articles allow exemption on dividends paid from income subject to full CIT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief on dividend distributions: (1) the non-resident recipient must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the tax authority of its residence jurisdiction for the relevant calendar year; (2) the WFOE must file Form 501 ('Application Form for Treaty Benefits') with the local tax bureau at least 10 working days before the distribution date; (3) the shareholder must provide legal entity chart, board resolution approving distribution, shareholder register, audited financial statements demonstrating that the recipient is not a conduit or shell, plus a Beneficial Ownership Declaration under SAT Public Notice [2018] No. 9; (4) the tax bureau will issue a written 'Treaty Benefit Approval' confirming the applicable rate; (5) the WFOE then deducts the treaty-reduced WHT on the actual dividend remittance. If the application is denied, the full 10% statutory WHT is deducted and an overpayment refund claim may be filed within 3 years under TCAL Art. 51.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT: interest and royalties paid to non-residents are both subject to 10% WHT (EIT Law Art. 3, 37). DTA rates vary: interest may be reduced to 7% (e.g., China-Hong Kong DTA) or even 0% when paid to an unrelated financial institution or the government of the other state as defined in the treaty; royalties are commonly reduced to 5% for patents, trademarks, industrial know-how, and copyrighted software, and 7% for rentals of industrial/commercial equipment. Relief is granted only upon presentation of the TRC and a domestic withholding agent filing the same treaty application protocol as for dividends, with written confirmation before the payment is wired abroad. Documentation must include the intellectual property ownership chain, license agreement consistent with the arm's-length principle, and proof that the IP was not merely transferred out of China to manufacture a treaty reduction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: RMB. Local transfer pricing documentation (Local File) must be prepared and maintained if, in the fiscal year, any of the following thresholds is exceeded: (a) aggregate related-party tangible asset purchases/sales > RMB 200 million; (b) aggregate related-party intangible property transfers > RMB 100 million; (c) aggregate intercompany financing including loans, guarantees, fund deposits > RMB 100 million; (d) aggregate other related-party transactions (services, cost-sharing) > RMB 40 million. Master File (Group File) is mandatory when the group's aggregate annual related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion or the WFOE is the party to cross-border related-party transactions exceeding RMB 100 million and belongs to an MNEG filing the group file. Country-by-Country Reporting thresholds follow BEPS action 13 for groups with consolidated revenue above RMB 5.5 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not maintain a standalone 'Economic Substance Regulations' (ESR) statute as in the UAE. However, the Economic Substance Doctrine is enforceable through: (i) the general anti-avoidance rule in EIT Law Art. 47, enabling tax authorities to re-characterize arrangements with no purpose other than tax avoidance; (ii) the 2018 Beneficial Ownership Standard (SAT Public Notice [2018] No. 9) requiring treaty claimants to show substantive business activity, (iii) the 'substance over form' doctrine applied in transfer pricing audits, and (iv) anti-money-laundering verification of 'beneficial owner' for all SPAC escrow and trust payments. For a SPAC WFOE, Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) include the management and oversight of the escrow/trust fund, the due diligence and negotiation for target acquisition, board approval of acquisition agreements, investment decisions regarding the listing proceeds, and ongoing Compliance Officer functions. Failure to perform CIGA in China, with only nominal staff and a mailbox address, will cause treaty benefits to be denied, the trust profits to be re-sourceable to China, and the WFOE to be considered a transparent shell for CIT and AML purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company with No Economic Substance and False Beneficial Ownership Claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Chinese WFOE-SPAC solely as a letterbox entity, with no office lease, zero local personnel, no board minutes, and all trust/escrow control exercised by foreign sponsors; obtaining a 5% treaty dividend rate by inserting a Hong Kong intermediary that performs no independent function and is merely a pass-through agent for the U.S. sponsor shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: EIT Law Article 47 (GAAR) allows the tax authority to recharacterize the inserted Hong Kong entity as fiscally transparent, deny treaty benefits, and impute all trust investment income and sponsor fees to the Chinese WFOE. The recharacterization imposes tax at 25% ordinary rate plus late interest and credits; under Tax Collection Administration Law Art. 63, a penalty of 50%-5x the additional tax found due may be imposed. Off-shore resale through a shell may also trigger Art. 26 of the Tax Law on the Administration of Tax Collection requiring payment before relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally and severally liable for the WFOE's unpaid CIT if the company is used to defraud creditors and tax; courts will pierce the corporate veil under Civil Law Principles (Art. 20 of the Civil Code) when abuse of legal personality is proven. Directors have been blacklisted (entry and exit prohibition) under TCAL Article 44, their personal bank accounts attached, and if they execute fabricated shareholder resolutions, they face up to 7 years' imprisonment for tax evasion under Criminal Law Art. 201. Personal fines up to RMB 500,000 can be imposed in serious fraud cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Criminal Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Transfer Pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating taxable income by (1) omitting trust interest or sponsor fees received, (2) paying inflated management fees or royalties to a non-resident related SPV without performing verifiable services or IP transfers, (3) using two sets of books for the SPAC accounts, or (4) failing to file Schedule A105000 related-party transaction disclosure after crossing RMB thresholds. Any of these attacks the reality of the WFOE's taxable presence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Collection Administration Law Art. 63: mandatory penalty of 50%-5x of the underpaid tax, plus daily 0.05% late surcharge. The Special Tax Adjustment framework under EIT Law Art. 41 opens audit exposure for 10 years (if thargeted) and requires interest assessed on the adjustment. Criminal Law Art. 201: where the evaded amount exceeds RMB 100,000 and is more than 10% of the tax that should be paid, the company's legal representative and other directly responsible supervisors can be convicted of tax evasion, punishable by up to 3 years' imprisonment and fines (for minor amounts) up to 7 years' imprisonment and fine for major amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and CFOs who signed false tax returns may be individually criminally prosecuted under Art. 201, notwithstanding company liquidation, with imprisonment of 3-7 years depending on the amount. The tax authority can attach personal assets for the portion of tax unpaid if the company is dissolved without paying; travel bans and 'Serious Tax Dishonesty' blacklisting are published. Civil restoration of the tax underpaid is a precondition to suspension or reduction of criminal sentence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Breach in SPAC Escrow Fund Flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routeing undisclosed third-party investments through the WFOE's escrow and trust accounts to mask the true beneficial owner of the SPAC; back-to-back loans or unsecured advances to non-resident officers without economic justification; failing to submit a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) under PRC AML rules; circumventing SAFE foreign exchange controls on outbound dividend or capital repatriation by netting of cross-border bookings or engaging in crypto-currency layering for trust contributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law (revised 2022), Articles 48-49 impose administrative fines: for institutions up to RMB 10 million (or 5% of the transaction amount) for serious failure in AML obligations; direct responsible persons face personal fines up to RMB 200,000. The State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) can impose penalties of 0.5%-1x illegal outward remittance and order repayment. Criminal Law Art. 191 (Money Laundering), as amended, criminalizes the concealment of proceeds from tax evasion, fraud, securities crime, or corruption: imprisonment for 5-10 years plus a fine for individuals; asset confiscation of the criminally derived proceeds and any laundering vehicles.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the WFOE are statutorily liable for AML compliance. Failure to appoint an AML compliance officer and program can give rise to personal fines of RMB 50,000-200,000 per infraction. Directors who personally authorize or execute the layering of escrow funds through multiple non-resident accounts commit a predicate offence to money laundering and face 5-10 years' imprisonment, revocation of the business license of the SPAC, and civil restitution for the full value of tainted proceeds. The travel ban applies and the tax bureau will coordinate with the public security and customs agencies to blacklist and extradite the principals.
